root_cause.text: The `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()` function unconditionally overwrites `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` with a newly acquired nfsd_file without releasing the existing reference, and stores the same nfsd_file pointer in both `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` and `fp->fi_rdeleg_file` with only a single reference count, causing reference leaks when the delegation is released.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch shows two critical fixes:

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by adding missing nfsd_file_put() call for read delegation file before access cleanup.
intent_record.what: Added a missing `nfsd_file_put(rnf)` call inside the `if (rnf)` block, and wrapped the conditional block with braces to contain both the new call and the existing `nfs4_file_put_access()` call.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that when a read delegation file (`rnf`) exists, it is properly released via `nfsd_file_put(rnf)` before calling `nfs4_file_put_access()`. Previously, the file reference was not being decremented, potentially causing a resource leak. The braces clarify the scope of the conditional block.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential file descriptor leak and reference counting issue by guarding against redundant assignments and properly managing nfsd_file lifecycle with get/put semantics.
intent_record.what: Modified the file descriptor assignment logic by: (1) removing a redundant `fp = stp->st_stid.sc_file` assignment, (2) wrapping `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` assignment in a conditional check, (3) setting `nf = NULL` after assignment, (4) changing `fp->fi_rdeleg_file` assignment to use `nfsd_file_get()` on the already-assigned descriptor, and (5) adding a post-unlock cleanup that calls `nfsd_file_put(nf)` if `nf` is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: This change prevents overwriting an already-assigned read-only file descriptor and ensures proper reference counting. The conditional check guards against redundant assignments to `fi_fds[O_RDONLY]`. The `nfsd_file_get()` call increments the reference count for the delegation file, and the deferred `nfsd_file_put()` call releases the original reference if it was not consumed by the assignment, preventing resource leaks and use-after-free issues.

grouping_result.intent: Fix potential file descriptor leak and reference counting issue by guarding against redundant assignments and properly managing nfsd_file lifecycle with get/put semantics.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix file descriptor and reference counting leaks by properly managing nfsd_file lifecycle with get/put semantics and preventing redundant assignments.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the core vulnerability by fixing reference counting leaks in nfsd_file lifecycle management. Hunk 0 adds the missing nfsd_file_put() call to release existing references before cleanup, and Hunk 1 prevents redundant assignments and ensures proper get/put semantics - both of which are the exact issues described in the root cause where fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] was being overwritten without releasing existing references and the same pointer was stored in multiple locations with insufficient reference counts.

candidates.rationale: This line unconditionally overwrites fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] without releasing the existing reference, causing a reference leak when there was a pre-existing nfsd_file pointer.

This line stores the same nfsd_file pointer (nf) in both fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] and fp->fi_rdeleg_file with only a single reference count, causing reference leaks when the delegation is released since both pointers reference the same object but only one reference was acquired.

This line acquires only a single reference count for the nfsd_file (nf), but the same pointer is then stored in two different locations (fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] and fp->fi_rdeleg_file), leading to insufficient reference counting for the dual usage.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally overwrites fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] without releasing any existing reference, causing a reference leak when a pre-existing nfsd_file pointer was already stored at this location.

This statement stores the same nfsd_file pointer (nf) in fp->fi_rdeleg_file after it was already stored in fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]. Since only a single reference was acquired via __nfs4_file_get_access(), storing the same pointer in two locations causes reference leaks when either location is released, as both will attempt to decrement the same reference count.

This statement acquires only a single reference count for the nfsd_file, but the same nfsd_file pointer is subsequently stored in two different locations (fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] and fp->fi_rdeleg_file), resulting in insufficient reference counting for the dual usage pattern and causing reference leaks.
